sources.articleTitle: No relief for motorists as fuel prices remain unchanged

headline: Energy Regulator Maintains Current Fuel Prices In Kenya Monthly Review
metaDescription: The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority has kept fuel prices steady in its latest review, leaving costs for petrol, diesel, and kerosene unchanged.
aiSummaryBullets: The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority announced that fuel prices will stay at current levels in Nairobi.
Petrol will continue to retail at Sh226.96 per litre for motorists.
Diesel and kerosene prices remain fixed at Sh227.76 and Sh219.87 per litre respectively.
aiContextParagraph: The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) is the government body responsible for overseeing the energy sector in Kenya, including the periodic adjustment of fuel prices. In its most recent review released in mid-November 2026, the authority determined that there would be no changes to the retail costs of fuel products. This decision maintains the price of petrol at Sh226.96 per litre, diesel at Sh227.76 per litre, and kerosene at Sh219.87 per litre within Nairobi. According to the regulatory body, this stability is intended to provide a cushion for consumers against potential market fluctuations. These prices remain applicable until the next review cycle initiated by the agency. This regulatory framework is standard practice in Kenya to manage the impact of global oil price volatility on domestic consumers, though this specific announcement offers no adjustment to the existing cost structure for Kenyan motorists and households relying on these fuels.
whyItIsViral: The story is trending due to high public search interest regarding fuel costs, reflecting significant consumer concern over transport and living expenses.
